title: Australia Skilled Migration Visa 2026: 189, 190 & 491 Guide
metaDescription: Australia skilled migration 2026: subclass 189, 190 and 491 points, skills assessment, 65-point minimum, fees and the step-by-step process today.
headline: Australia Skilled Migration Visa 2026: Complete Guide

sections.title: Skilled Migration Pathways
sections.content:
Australia's General Skilled Migration program runs through SkillSelect and offers three main visas: subclass 189 for independent permanent residence, subclass 190 for state-nominated permanent residence, and subclass 491 for regional provisional residence leading to permanent residence. For 2026-27, Australia has set 21,090 places for the 189 and 35,500 for the state-nominated 190 visa, with 58,040 places for employer-sponsored visas.

All three pathways require an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list, a positive skills assessment, and at least 65 points. In practice, invitations usually go to applicants with higher scores because places are limited. The 189 grants permanent residence immediately, while the 491 is a five-year provisional visa with a pathway to permanent residence.

sections.title: The Points Test
sections.content:
Points are awarded for age, qualifications, work experience, English ability and other factors. Applicants aged 25 to 32 receive the maximum age points, a bachelor's degree earns 15 points, and superior English earns 20 points. Australian work experience and Australian study add further points, and state nomination adds 5 points for the 190 or 15 points for the 491.

Applicants must be under 45, meet English, health and character requirements, and hold an occupation on the relevant list. If your occupation is not on the list, you cannot proceed through SkillSelect for that visa. A provincial or state nomination can substantially improve your chances of receiving an invitation.

sections.title: Skills Assessment and English
sections.content:
Every applicant needs a skills assessment from the body relevant to their occupation. IT workers are assessed by the Australian Computer Society, engineers by Engineers Australia, and trades workers by Trades Recognition Australia. The assessment confirms that your qualifications and experience meet Australian standards.

Accepted English tests include IELTS, PTE and TOEFL. Competent English is the minimum, but higher scores earn more points and are often needed to reach a competitive total. Tests must be taken at an approved centre within the required validity period, so plan your test date early in the process.

sections.title: Fees, Timelines and Steps
sections.content:
The visa fee for the subclass 189 is AUD 6,135 for the main applicant. After receiving an invitation, you have 60 days to lodge a complete application. Processing usually takes 6 to 18 months depending on the subclass and the complexity of the case.

The steps are: check your occupation is on the list, obtain your skills assessment, sit your English test, submit an Expression of Interest, wait for an invitation, then lodge the visa application with health and character documents. Always confirm current fees and occupation lists on the Department of Home Affairs website before applying.

faqs.q: What is the minimum points score for Australian skilled migration?
faqs.a: The minimum score to lodge an Expression of Interest is 65 points. In practice, invitations often go to applicants with higher scores because places are limited and competition is strong. Points are awarded for age, qualifications, work experience, English ability and other factors. State or territory nomination adds points and improves your chances of receiving an invitation through SkillSelect.

faqs.q: What is the difference between visas 189, 190 and 491?
faqs.a: The 189 is an independent permanent residence visa that needs no state or employer sponsorship. The 190 requires state nomination and grants permanent residence immediately. The 491 is a five-year regional provisional visa that leads to permanent residence after meeting income and residence conditions. All three use the SkillSelect points system and require a positive skills assessment.

faqs.q: How long does Australian skilled migration take?
faqs.a: Processing usually takes 6 to 18 months, depending on the subclass and the complexity of the case. After receiving an invitation through SkillSelect, you have 60 days to lodge a complete application. Applications with health and character documents ready at lodgement are generally processed faster. Planning ahead and preparing documents early can save months of waiting.

faqs.q: Do I need a skills assessment for Australian migration?
faqs.a: Yes, a positive skills assessment is mandatory for all General Skilled Migration visas. The assessing body depends on your occupation: the Australian Computer Society for IT workers, Engineers Australia for engineers, and Trades Recognition Australia for trades. The assessment verifies that your qualifications and work experience meet Australian standards before you can submit an Expression of Interest.
